It’s an exciting time to join Netflix as we continue to bring new stories to audiences around the world and expand how we work with brands and advertisers. Strategic partnerships and our advertising business create new opportunities to connect brands with entertainment, fandom, and engaged audiences.


Netflix works with brands and advertisers to create partnerships that bring our stories into culture in new ways. In Korea, the Marketing Partnerships Creative team leads the creative work behind these collaborations, connecting partner objectives, audience insights, and Netflix titles to develop campaigns that people want to engage with and talk about.


We’re looking for a Marketing Partnerships Creative Manager to lead this work from strategy through execution. The role spans two connected areas: consumer-facing campaigns created with brand partners and distribution partners, and B2B marketing and creative work that communicates the value of Netflix Ads to advertisers and agencies. This includes shaping compelling narratives, sales materials, and industry experiences that demonstrate how brands can connect with audiences through Netflix. Across both areas, you’ll translate business objectives into distinctive creative work grounded in a strong understanding of our brand, content, and audiences.


The role


You will work closely with Brand Partnerships / Partner Marketing Leads to identify opportunities, shape proposals, and lead the creative development of partnership campaigns. You’ll be involved from the earliest conversations: understanding a partner’s business challenge, finding a compelling role for Netflix and its titles, developing a strategic brief, and guiding the idea through production and launch.


You will be a partner-facing creative lead, working directly with advertisers and their agencies while bringing together teams across Netflix. You’ll lead briefings, workshops, presentations, and creative reviews; give clear direction and feedback; and ensure the final work delivers on its strategic intent, meets a high standard of creative excellence, and brings the Netflix brand and our titles to life in compelling ways.


You will also lead creative work that supports the Ads business, including pitch narratives, case studies, sales materials, and selected industry events and large-scale initiatives. This calls for someone who can move between big-picture thinking and hands-on delivery, managing multiple projects without losing sight of the idea.


Key responsibilities

  • Develop partnership opportunities and strategy. Explore Netflix titles and audiences to identify opportunities for partners. Connect partner objectives, consumer behavior, and cultural insights to create briefs, concepts, and presentations that can be pitched and developed into campaigns.
  • Lead campaigns end to end. Own creative strategy and development from the initial brief through ideation, planning, production, and execution. Ensure the campaign narrative remains clear and the work meets its business and creative objectives.
  • Lead the creative process with partners and agencies. Run workshops, briefings, presentations, and review sessions. Set direction, manage the feedback loop, and constructively challenge collaborators to make the work more distinctive and effective.
  • Oversee creative execution. Direct the development and delivery of campaign assets across relevant formats and channels. Manage creative and design agencies, vendors, and bespoke productions or shoots when needed.
  • Develop creative work for Ads marketing. Shape pitch narratives and lead the development of sales enablement materials, including presentations, video, print, social content, and case studies. Ensure the work communicates a compelling story, meets a high creative standard, and is reviewed, approved, and delivered on time.
  • Lead creative operations for major initiatives. Manage the creative workstream for selected Ads industry events and large-scale projects, including creative strategy and concepting, agency engagement, workflows, timelines, budgets, production, and coordination across teams.
  • Build alignment and protect the work. Partner closely with internal creative, marketing, sales, legal, and other relevant teams to navigate approvals and clearances. Ensure the Netflix brand and owned or licensed titles are represented and used appropriately throughout partner and Ads creative.

Qualifications and experience


  • 12+ years of experience in brand or consumer marketing, with substantial experience leading creative development at an advertising or integrated agency. In-house brand marketing / creative experience is a strong plus.
  • A proven ability to independently lead complex, integrated campaigns from brief and strategy through creative development, production, and launch.
  • Strong strategic thinking, with the ability to draw connections between business objectives, consumer research, behavior, culture, and content to find fertile ground for creative ideas.
  • Strong creative instincts and a media-agnostic approach. You can contribute ideas, shape and pitch concepts, write compelling briefs, and guide agencies toward work that feels fresh rather than expected.
  • Experience building trusted relationships with external partners and agencies, and aligning and influencing stakeholders across a complex, matrixed organization. You can navigate different organizational structures, dynamics, and working styles, adapting your communication with clarity, sound judgment, and diplomacy.
  • Solid production knowledge and project management skills. You can manage several workstreams, get into the details when needed, and solve problems while protecting the broader strategic intent.
  • Fluency in Korean and English, with the ability to communicate clearly and persuasively with internal teams and external senior stakeholders.
  • A deep understanding of the Korean market and the role cultural relevance plays in effective marketing. Experience in entertainment, content, or advertising partnerships is a plus.
  • Strong English proficiency; experience communicating and working with global teams and stakeholders is a plus.

How you work


You’re curious about entertainment and have a genuine interest in how people connect with stories, brands, and culture. You bring a point of view while staying open to other perspectives, and you know how to give and receive candid, constructive feedback.


You take ownership without needing a large team around you. You understand how to work across different organizations and working styles, communicate with judgment and diplomacy, and roll up your sleeves to move work forward when the path is unclear. You’re comfortable adapting as the business evolves and can thrive in Netflix’s culture of freedom and responsibility.

The Title Producer team serves as the single point of accountability for the end-to-end localisation process across all assigned titles in their country or slate. Job Summary:

We are seeking a Head of Cinematography, Lighting to support our upcoming film. This role is responsible for overseeing the cinematic vision and visual storytelling of the film through a lighting lens. The Head of Cinematography, Lighting works inside of NAS to lead the Lighting department and ensure the visual quality, consistency, and continuity of lighting across the production, shaping mood, atmosphere, and readability in every shot.

The Head of Cinematography, Lighting will collaborate closely with the Director, VFX Supervisor, Production Designer, Art Directors, Head of Cinematography, Layout, and other department heads to define the film’s lighting style and integrate it with camera, design, and character performance. They will guide the Lighting team through look development and shot production, providing creative and technical feedback, while helping to design workflows and tools that support efficient, high-quality output.


What You’ll Do:

  • Partner with the Director, VFX Supervisor, Production Designer, and Art Directors to define the film’s lighting style and ensure it aligns with the overall visual direction
  • Collaborate closely with the Head of Cinematography, Layout to build a unified cinematic language that integrates camera, lighting, and composition
  • Lead and mentor Lighting Supervisors, Leads, and Artists, setting expectations and providing creative and technical feedback in dailies and reviews
  • Review and approve lighting work, maintaining continuity and quality standards across sequences and shots
  • Partner with Modeling, Surfacing, Environments, FX, CFX, and Compositing to ensure seamless integration of assets and effects into final lit and composited images
  • Oversee the creation and maintenance of lighting rigs, templates, and workflows that support efficiency and consistency across the show
  • Collaborate with CG/Technical Supervisors, Production Technology, and R&D on pipeline developments, tool needs, and the technical feasibility of lighting concepts
  • Troubleshoot and resolve escalated lighting-related technical issues with TDs and engineering partners
  • Work closely with Production Management to bid, schedule, and track lighting work, ensuring milestones are met on time and within budget
  • Encourage a collaborative atmosphere by promoting respect, integrity, inclusion, and trust, and support training and development initiatives for Lighting artists

What You’ll Need:


  • Proven experience as a Supervisor or Head of Lighting on animated feature films or similar high‑end animation/VFX projects
  • Several years of experience in leadership or supervisory roles in film, TV, or games, backed by 10+ years in lighting/lookdev/comp craft preferred
  • A reel/portfolio demonstrating excellence in lighting, colour, mood, and cinematic storytelling

  • Work closely with Assets, Layout, Environments, Effects, CFX, Lighting, and Compositing to ensure crowds integrate seamlessly into shots and support hero action and readability.
  • Help define and refine crowd tools, workflows, and libraries in partnership with Technical Supervisors, crowds TDs, and pipeline teams.
  • Provide input to Production Management and department leadership on crowds complexity and progress to support realistic planning and prioritization.
  • Troubleshoot technical and artistic challenges in crowds work, collaborating on solutions that maintain quality while meeting schedule needs.

About the Organization

Platform Modernization Engineering (PME) helps keep Netflix's engineering fleet healthy, secure, and current. We design and run the large-scale migration and modernization campaigns that move the fleet forward — from dependency upgrades to infrastructure-level changes — so that individual engineering teams don't have to absorb that toil on their own.



About the Team and the Role

The Change Systems team owns the platforms that make fleet-wide change possible at Netflix.  It gives engineering teams across the company a unified way to scope, launch, automate, and validate change at scale — from routine dependency updates to complex, multi-service migrations — with as little manual toil as possible.

The platform already operates at significant scale: over 100 engineering teams run change activities across thousands of repositories, and usage continues to grow year over year. The team's mandate is expanding to match — pushing automation further using AI-assisted code modification, rule-based transformations, and batch orchestration. The goal is to make the majority of change at Netflix low-to-no-effort for the engineers on the receiving end, while giving the teams driving that change the tooling, telemetry, and adoption data they need to move with confidence.


You will lead the engineers who build and operate this platform, based in Warsaw. This is a team with deep end-to-end ownership: they run their own on-call, design the automation and orchestration layers directly, and are pushing the platform toward AI-driven code transformation as a first-class capability rather than a one-off tool. 



End-to-end ownership translates into several responsibilities:

  • From a technical perspective, acting like a System Architect, driving technical architecture and component integration; 
  • From a product perspective, wearing the Product Manager hat for Campaigns and defining the vision and strategy for the Campaigns experience; 
  • From a partnership and stakeholders' perspective, identifying needs, incorporating feedback, aligning across the organization, creating partnerships to drive impact
  • From a leadership perspective, acting like a Change Agent and Advocate supporting the overall organization in shaping the mindset and approach around Campaigns (change at scale) in the agentic world; 



The platform is at an inflection point, which makes this role particularly important:

  • From tooling to platform. Change Systems has built strong point solutions for individual campaigns. The next step is composable, declarative abstractions that every part of the platform — and the teams building on top of it — share a common foundation rather than one-off automation.
  • From manual campaign design to AI-assisted execution. GenAI-driven code transformation, contract-based validation, and batch orchestration are becoming core to how campaigns get executed — across code transformation, CI, testing, and delivery to production.
  • From reactive to metrics-driven prioritization. Using historical campaign completion data to predict bottlenecks, target specific automation investments, and measure adoption and adherence rather than simply responding to inbound requests.
  • From isolated campaigns to a coherent customer experience. Close technical alignment is required with Source Management, Continuous Integration, Resilience Engineering and Delivery Engineering and Security so that campaign recipients experience one coherent platform, not a patchwork of tools.



What You Will Do

  • Be a thought partner to Organization Champions, Campaign Managers, Campaign Recipients, and engineering leadership in setting the vision, strategy, and adoption path for fleet-wide change management as a platform capability.
  • Own the technical architecture direction for a composable, declarative platform that generalizes beyond any single migration use case.
  • Serve as a credible technical advisor to your team, helping engineers navigate ambiguous, cross-domain technical decisions — and act as the team's escalation point for novel campaigns that span multiple technical domains.
  • Drive AI-first ways of working across the team: treat AI-assisted code modification as core infrastructure, and advance agent-assisted engineering practices with the code review, change-risk management, testing, and evaluation rigor required to run them safely at scale.
  • Raise the team's rigor around impact — define meaningful adoption and adherence metrics, use historical campaign data to predict and target automation investment, and prioritize based on evidence rather than only inbound requests.
  • Own the operational excellence of a platform relied on across the fleet, including on-call responsibilities, telemetry and dashboards for fleet health, and feedback loops that continuously improve campaign design and execution.
  • Communicate complex technical and product tradeoffs clearly, in writing and verbally, to influence decisions across a broad set of stakeholders — including technical executives, SREs, and security incident commanders.
  • Lead, hire, coach, and develop a team of engineers; challenge them to expand their ownership and grow their impact beyond their immediate scope.
  • Foster a strong culture of accountability, and build an inclusive team environment where every engineer feels empowered to contribute at their best.



What We Are Looking For

  • Experience building and operating platform systems that support large-scale, business-critical use cases, including on-call responsibilities and resilient, well-instrumented services.
  • Strong technical acumen in distributed systems and developer platforms, with the ability to move between architecture and implementation detail, and to represent technical decisions credibly to partner teams.
  • Experience building and leading inclusive engineering teams, attracting and retaining talent, and fostering a culture where individuals take ownership while contributing to shared outcomes.
  • Strong long-term strategic thinking and a platform mindset — able to define a technical vision for composable, extensible systems and connect it to broader organizational goals.
  • Proven ability to navigate ambiguity, influence without authority, and partner effectively with senior stakeholders across engineering, product, and security.
  • Rigor in decision-making: comfortable reducing ambiguity through a mix of data, stakeholder input, constructive dissent, and targeted experiments.
  • Fluency with AI-assisted engineering, with a clear point of view on how to adopt GenAI-driven code transformation and agentic tooling safely at scale.
  • Strong technical writing skills — design docs, tradeoff analyses, postmortems — and a track record of driving complex, cross-functional technical projects from design through completion.



Nice to Have

  • Experience with large-scale code migration or modernization campaigns.
  • Experience building or operating fleet-management, dependency graph, or service catalog systems.
  • Background in platform or infrastructure engineering organizations.
  • Familiarity with Java or Python in a backend services context.
  • Experience designing platforms where agents, not just humans, are first-class consumers — including provisioning and debugging through APIs rather than a UI.
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred: EC2, S3, EKS/Kubernetes).

About the team


The Validation & Safety Platform is one of three pillars inside the new System Health, Validation & Insights Platform group in Productivity Engineering. Our mandate: catch safety and correctness regressions in human-written or agent-generated code before they reach production.


Netflix's agent fleet now writes, tests, refactors, and deploys code continuously across every domain. As agent volume grows, the constraint shifts from producing changes to knowing which ones are safe. Quality assurance can no longer be a human-gated step at the end of a PR — it has to be embedded at every stage of the developer loop, proactive and automated.


Today the team runs the validation and safety gates for the fleet: automated test generation, coverage and safeguards show teams where they stand. We're extending to other safety signals built specifically for agent-generated code, so we can judge whether a change is genuinely correct as agents write and modify code at scale.


About the role


We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build the next generation of this platform: tools and guardrails that keep pace with an engineering org where a growing share of code is agent-generated.


You will design systems that thousands of engineers and their agents depend on, make build-vs-extend calls on what the platform should own versus expose through an API, and bring a security-conscious view to how autonomous agents get sandboxed, scoped, and safely given access to test infrastructure.


Key responsibilities


  • Design and build validation and safety products used platform-wide: test generation, coverage and safeguards, deterministic and predictive test selection, and mutation testing at scale.
  • Build the polyglot static analysis layer that gives agent-generated code an automated, language-agnostic first quality gate.
  • Develop agent-specific safety signals: detect prompt flakiness (an agent producing inconsistent output across identical prompts or seeds), evaluate agent trajectories against execution traces, and score semantic correctness of agent-generated code against the original requirement, the agent's own stated intent, and observed behavior change.
  • Define clear platform capabilities and make deliberate build-vs-buy, build-vs-extend calls as the platform's scope grows.
  • Apply sound judgment on agent sandboxing, scoping, and data redaction wherever the platform gives agents access to test infrastructure or execution environments.

Who you are


  • Experienced building and operating a platform used by other engineering teams — you think about your product as a platform, not a one-off tool.
  • Comfortable making product calls: what capability the platform should own, what it should expose as an API, and when to extend versus build new.
  • An advanced user of agentic coding tools — you work daily with hooks, MCPs, and context management, even if you haven't built an agentic platform yourself.
  • Security-minded: you have a working understanding of agent sandboxing, scoping, and redaction, even if it isn't your primary background.
  • A strong communicator who can document technical tradeoffs clearly for both engineering and non-technical stakeholders.
  • An advocate for a strong testing culture: familiar with test frameworks, code coverage tooling, CI systems, and post-deployment verification.

Experience we'd be excited about


  • You have designed or operated developer-platform infrastructure: distribution, CI/CD, or versioning systems used by many teams.
  • You have built or integrated LLM-based evaluation systems (LLM-as-judge, agent trajectory scoring, or similar).
  • You have worked with mutation testing, static analysis, or test-selection systems at scale.
  • You have hands-on experience sandboxing or scoping agent access to sensitive systems or data.

The Environment Modeling Lead is responsible for leading a team of environment modeling artists whilst working closely with the Supervisor to realize their vision, ensuring the standard and quality of work produced is consistently high.
 

What You’ll Do:

Creative Responsibilities

  • Ensure a high level of communication is maintained with the Supervisor and production management particularly where situations arise that may compromise the quality or scheduled delivery of material. This may include overseeing and reporting on particular aspects of a project and identifying and implementing solutions as problems arise.

  • Interpret 2D designs and translate them into 3D space by utilizing software such as Maya, ZBrush, or Houdini, all while maintaining the original artistic intent.

  • Assume responsibility for ensuring assigned work is produced to appropriate standard quality within the scheduled timeframe and deadline. 

  • Produce highly optimized meshes that can be rendered and displayed efficiently for downstream departments.

  • Produce accurate UVs for models for use in downstream departments.

  • Produce complex models to a high standard with a thorough understanding of shape, scale and form.

  • Work within/produce topology/wireframe.

  • Produce accurate UVs for models for use in downstream departments.

  • Produce highly optimized meshes that can be rendered and displayed efficiently for downstream departments such as Rigging, Layout and Lighting.

  • Regularly distribute and share knowledge to support the ongoing development of innovative tools and/or techniques for Modelling.

  • Interact with tracking systems and production staff.

Lead Duties

  • Leads a team under guidance from the Head of Environment, Environment Modeling Supervisor and production team.

  • Provide day‑to‑day leadership and work with Production and Artist Management to develop the skills and abilities of all artists in the team.

  • Mentor less‑experienced artists, providing both creative and technical guidance.

  • Understands the overall project brief and goals and communicates them clearly to each team member.

  • Delegates work responsibly to ensure the successful completion of shots across team members of all skill levels.

  • Drive team reviews and offer constructive, creative and technical feedback on work in progress.

  • Perform daily one‑on‑one rounds with artists to track progress and support problem‑solving.

  • Communicates production information to both the artists group and Production Management.

  • Participates in production pipeline problem-solving.

  • Documents new techniques and distributes updates to peers, crew and Production Management.

  • Prioritise and break down a project into organized parts.

  • Support open communication between your department, R&D and all other departments.

  • Work with the Environment Modeling Supervisor and production team to prepare bids and pitches as required.

  • Participate in the recruiting and interview process for new employees as required.

  • Assist Production Management in preparation of final show reports as required.

 This role is based in Vancouver, British Columbia. Hybrid Role (Minimum of 3 days a week in the office).

The Role:

Netflix is looking for a Coordinator to join the Production Management team supporting Indonesia titles. This person will support productions from early planning through delivery, working closely with the Production Management team, other Netflix teams, and outside partners.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys detail, moves fast, and is comfortable talking directly with senior producers about budgets, schedules, and workflows. The right person has real Line Producer experience and can work independently.

How We Work

Our content strategy starts with Creativity — generating new ideas. Innovation is turning those ideas into results that matter, and always pushing to do better than before. Risk-Taking is what makes Innovation possible.

Creativity without Risk-Taking stays safe and eventually runs out of bold ideas. Risk-Taking without Creativity leads to bets made without real thought. We need both, working together, to build Innovation — and Innovation is what turns single good moments into lasting momentum for the business.

Responsibilities

  • Support Production Management Managers/Executives in onboarding and running original film and series productions Indonesia

  • Act as the day-to-day link between productions and internal Netflix teams, making sure information moves quickly and accurately both ways.

  • Serve as an in-house Line Producer across pre-production, production, and post-production — reviewing budgets, schedules, and workflows, Research and reach out to potential filming locations and studios.

  • Communicate and negotiate directly with senior producers on budget, schedule, and production plan questions.

  • Build and maintain production schedules, and share updates so all teams stay aligned.

  • Create, organize, and maintain production documents and internal databases (schedules, crew, contacts).

  • Schedule, coordinate, and attend production meetings.

  • Manage relationships with Production Partners and vendors — gather feedback, work with manager to help production partner improve, and track cost efficiency.

  • Research and reach out to potential filming locations and studios.

  • Help identify and vet strong production staff and crew, and coordinate onboarding for production companies and freelance producers.

  • Handle travel and logistics for the team and for set visits.

  • Respect and understand local ways of working (with Production Partners and local crews) while making sure everything stays aligned with Netflix's standards and values.

  • Spot small operational problems early and fix them before they grow into bigger issues.

  • Provide translation and interpretation support in company workshop or initiatives as needed.

  • Stay current on new production tools and technology, and bring useful ones into the workflow.

Qualifications & How You Work

Experience & Skills

  • 3-5 years of experience as a Line Producer in film or series production.

  • Fluent in Indonesia  Plus English

  • Strong understanding of production budgets, schedules, and paperwork.

  • Comfortable in a fast-paced environment, supporting more than one project at a time.

  • Able to respond to urgent matters outside normal hours when needed.

  • Proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, and Google Suite. Familiarity with Movie Magic Budgeting/Scheduling is a plus, not required.

  • Willing to travel across the region to support productions.

Good Judgement

  • Lays out options and trade-offs clearly — quality vs. time vs. cost.

  • Comes to discussions prepared, with the right information to support a decision.

  • Acts as an engaged thought partner — shares risks honestly, without being judgmental.

Proactive Communication

  • Flags important risks early, before they become real problems.

  • Comfortable sharing candid opinions with the Content team.

  • Makes sure Production's point of view is actually heard in key decisions.

Curiosity

  • Asks thoughtful questions to fully understand context before acting.

  • Approaches discussions with an open mind and genuinely listens to other views.

  • Open to new ways of working when the reasoning behind them is solid.

Day-to-Day Strengths

  • Strong attention to detail — keeps schedules, documents, and logistics accurate.

  • Quick, practical problem-solving to avoid delays.

  • Takes ownership of tasks and sees them through.

  • Team player who supports Managers and colleagues to keep production moving smoothly.

  • Keeps information confidential when needed.

  • Genuine passion for entertainment and scripted content, with a drive to keep learning about production processes and new tools.

About the Role

The Screening Specialist owns end-to-end execution of physical and virtual screenings across APAC, acting as the technical and vendor-management expert who ensures every screening meets Netflix's quality bar, on time and on brand. This is a hands-on, in-market role requiring strong cross-functional relationship skills and hands-on project management, supported by technical screening expertise.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end execution of physical and virtual screenings, including DCP/KDM ingest, subtitle and audio configuration, and onsite or remote technical support.

  • Run the standard technical checklist: venue tech checks before screening day, content re-checks with PSCs before doors open, and standby coverage through the end of the screening, covering AV equipment, projector calibration, audio levels, framing, and safety hazards.

  • Manage day-to-day vendor relationships across the team's 19-vendor active roster spanning DCP creation, QC, tech check/on-site execution, engineering/buildout, and virtual-screening platforms.

  • Keep Glowbot (the team's project-tracking system) current and support ongoing efforts to automate manual admin work.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Publicity, Events, Post Production, and Awards on timing, asset readiness, and market-specific requirements (e.g. classification, versioning).

  • Build and manage vendor relationships across APAC, ensuring reliance on vendors; while helping diversify and strengthen the local vendor bench in each country.

  • Serve as the primary screening project point of contact, navigating language, quality, delivery and stakeholder complexity independently.

Requirements - Must Have

  • Strong project and time management, including composure under reactive, short-notice timelines.

  • Comfortable operating independently in-market; will often be the only Screenings presence in India day to day.

  • Cross-functional collaboration skills: this role sits at the intersection of Publicity, Events, and Post Production and needs to build trust with all three.

  • Stakeholder & Reputation Management: SME support for cross-functional enquiries; filmmaker/executive alignment on sensitive quality conversations.

  • High attention to detail and an excellence bar suited to premiere-level, talent-facing events.

  • Vendor Relationship Management: setting and enforcing service-level expectations with vendors and engineering contractors.

  • Admin: expense tracking, vendor payment system setup, Glowbot access setup.

  • Willing to travel.

Requirements - Preferred

  • Hands-on technical experience in DCI (Digital Cinema Initiatives) and AV: DCP, QC, tech check, and KDM technical understanding, plus real-time pass/fail judgment on site.

  • On-Site Execution: technical producing, day-of-event communication management, on-site vendor accountability.

  • Ability to read and enforce precise digital cinema equipment calibration standards.

  • Business acumen and a "quality gatekeeper" mindset, treating technical execution as a strategic contribution to campaign and awards outcomes, not just delivery.

  • Experience building or managing vendor relationships from scratch in a market, especially valuable given India's current vendor concentration risk.

  • Familiarity with festival or awards-season logistics.

  • Regional Operations: proven ability to manage multi-country logistics independently and adapt to local venue/market conditions.

What Success Looks Like

Screenings run smoothly and on-brand across all APAC markets; vendor relationships are proactively managed and diversified; and cross-functional partners see Screenings as a trusted, strategic partner, not just a technical service.

The Finance & Strategy function plays a pivotal role in developing Netflix’s strategy and supporting its execution. We are seeking an Associate for our EMEA Studio Strategy team based in London. The Netflix Studio is the largest in the world, overseeing the production of Netflix original series and films. Studio Strategy is a high-impact group within the wider Studio Finance organisation that works on strategic initiatives that cut across functions and markets. We partner with EMEA leaders across all areas of Production (production management, innovation, talent development, facilities), as well as wider Finance, Content and Legal teams. We provide strategic guidance on essential business decisions about how our content gets made, and ensure the Studio has the resources and operating models to deliver its long-term objectives. We also provide strategic support to the Labour Relations team (responsible for agreements with talent guilds and unions in the region), and oversee compliance with Netflix’s royalties and residuals obligations in EMEA. 

The Associate position will be an integral member of the strategy team, reporting to the Senior Manager, Studio F&S and working alongside one other F&S Manager. You will be responsible for providing support and analysis across the breadth of work provided by the team. This role will be based in Netflix's London office but will collaborate with teams across the EMEA region, as well as global stakeholders.

  • Build a deep understanding of industry trends, competitive threats and opportunities and share market intelligence internally

  • High aptitude and enthusiasm for complex problem solving, and experience conducting quantitative and qualitative analysis to generate insights using data

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to present complex analysis to executives/senior management clearly and concisely

Turntables, with wireframes, of character and creature models

As the UK Retail Senior Manager, you will own the strategy and execution of Netflix’s Consumer Products retail business across the UK, while also developing the broader EMEA retail strategy. With particular expertise in Hardlines, you will identify growth opportunities, build strategic retailer relationships and deliver best-in-class programmes across priority categories and franchises, while developing insights, strategies and best practices that can scale across EMEA.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the UK & Ireland retail strategy and execution, setting priorities across key channels, retailers and franchise opportunities.
  • Develop the EMEA retail strategy, bringing deep channel, category and retail expertise to identify regional priorities, growth opportunities and whitespace.
  • Identify UK & Ireland retail growth opportunities, using market intelligence, consumer insights and commercial data to shape investment and prioritisation.
  • Build and manage strategic relationships with priority UK & Ireland retailers, developing joint business plans and opportunities to grow Netflix’s Consumer Products presence, with a particular focus on Hardlines.
  • Partner with UK cross functional teams and licensees to maximise retail execution, including listings, assortment, placement, activation and in-store presence.
  • Translate global Consumer Products strategies into UK & Ireland and EMEA retail plans, ensuring global priorities are relevant to local market and retailer dynamics, while bringing Hardlines expertise where relevant.
  • Maximise major franchise and seasonal retail moments in the UK & Ireland, developing distinctive activations that deliver visibility, commercial impact and fan engagement.
  • Establish EMEA Hardlines best practice and capability, sharing UK & Ireland learnings and developing scalable approaches that can be adopted across markets.
  • Track and evaluate UK & Ireland retail performance, using sell-through, market and partner data to measure impact, identify opportunities and improve future programmes.
  • Build and manage strategic UK licensee partnerships, developing joint business plans, go-to-market strategies and effective account management.

What We’re Looking For

Must‑have

  • Significant experience in retail, consumer products, licensing or entertainment, with deep expertise in Hardlines, ideally toys.
  • Deep understanding of the UK & Ireland retail landscape, with broader knowledge of EMEA channels, markets and retail dynamics.
  • Proven experience developing and executing retail strategies that deliver measurable commercial growth.
  • Strong commercial judgement, with the ability to identify opportunities, prioritise investment and make clear decisions.
  • Experience translating global Consumer Products strategies into locally relevant retail plans, with the ability to operate across UK & Ireland execution and EMEA strategy.
  • Strong analytical skills, using retail performance, market intelligence and consumer insights to identify opportunities and inform decisions.
  • Highly effective communication, influencing and cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to align Licensing, Hardlines, Marketing, country teams and external partners and influence senior stakeholders.

Nice to have

  • Established relationships with senior UK retail stakeholders, particularly across buying, category management and retail marketing.
  • Experience working in or with entertainment brands and franchises.
  • Ability to work with a high degree of autonomy, constructively challenge existing approaches, identify new opportunities and drive change.
  • Genuine passion for entertainment, brands and retail, and an understanding of how fans engage with Netflix IP.

| Production Innovation

Our Production Innovation team drives industry innovation, sets technical standards, and provides direct production support across Netflix's global slate. We support creative teams, crews, post facilities, and internal partners - from capture through delivery - ensuring our workflows balance creative ambition with technical excellence. Beyond support, we actively explore emerging opportunities in AI, imaging/sound, and production technology, always grounded in real-world filmmaking practice.

| Role Overview

We are seeking a Director, Production Innovation to build and lead the team responsible for identifying, piloting, and scaling emerging production technology across APAC - including generative AI, on-set tools, and VFX/imaging workflow innovation. This leader sets the innovation roadmap, manages a team of technology managers (including the GenLab and GenTech), and is the primary point of contact with Product, Legal, and Content Operations to turn field pilots into org-wide guidance and standards. You bring a strong point of view on where technology can genuinely improve creative and production outcomes, the judgment to say no to hype, and the leadership skill to build a team that filmmakers and production partners trust.

| Key Responsibilities

  • Set and own the Production Innovation roadmap and prioritization across APAC, balancing AI, imaging, sound, and emerging technology opportunities against production impact.

  • Lead and grow the team, including direct management of the GenLab, GenTech, Production Technology, and other innovation roles - setting goals, coaching, and developing talent.

  • Partner with production and content leadership, directors, producers, and external creative leads to identify where new technology can meaningfully improve creative quality, speed, or cost.

  • Own the pilot-to-standard pipeline: run structured pilots, evaluate outcomes against traditional methods, and convert what works into scalable guidance, training, and vendor recommendations.

  • Represent the APAC Production with COI, Product, and legal, ensuring new workflows meet copyright, IP, and data security standards before they scale.

  • Build and maintain relationships across the vendor, studio, and talent ecosystem, spanning both generative and traditional production technologies.

  • Report progress, risk, and resourcing needs to senior leadership, and make the call on where to invest, pause, or kill a given pilot.

  • Champion field feedback from production teams into product and process improvements.

| Qualifications

Required:

  • 15+ years of experience in film/series/gaming/VFX production, including prior people leadership.

  • Demonstrated track record leading teams through the adoption of new production technology (AI or otherwise) - not solely an individual-contributor background.

  • Strong grasp of end-to-end production and post (from development and previs through VFX turnover, conform/online, and delivery), and where technology intersects with each stage.

  • Hands-on familiarity with generative AI tools as well as core production tools (Unreal Engine, Adobe Premiere), but not limited to.

  • Excellent executive communication skills; able to translate technical and creative tradeoffs for senior stakeholders and cross-functional partners.

  • Experience managing cross-functional partners (Product, Legal, Content Operations) and external vendor ecosystems.

Preferred:

  • Degree in design, film, technology, or a related field.

  • Experience building a team or function from the ground up.

  • Regional experience across APAC production markets.

  • Familiarity with copyright, IP, and data security considerations in AI-driven workflows.

  • Track record establishing vendor and freelance talent relationships in emerging production technology.

As Netflix grows, we keep advancing innovations in personalization and discovery, experimentation and decision-making, understanding our members and our titles, and backend infrastructure. These developments constantly create new opportunities for research to drive meaningful impact. By exploring the frontiers of AI/ML and intersecting fields, the Machine Learning and Inference Research team turns these opportunities into tangible benefits for our members and our business.

The Machine Learning and Inference Research team is a dedicated research team building up Netflix’s technical capabilities by tackling fundamental research questions tied to our most important challenges and partnering closely with teams across the business to translate research into impact at scale. As a member of the team, you will leverage your technical expertise to shape roadmaps, collaborate across functions, and bring new ideas from exploration to impact. You will also engage actively with the broader research community by publishing at top venues, presenting at conferences, mentoring interns, and fostering academic collaborations.

We are seeking an experienced researcher who can establish and execute a strong research agenda in AI alignment science, pursue both internal and external impact, disseminate knowledge effectively and inspire others, collaborate with colleagues to deliver tangible business value, and help foster an open environment of innovation, intellectual rigor, and curiosity. This role will pursue frontier, foundational research that shapes the direction of the field and influences how Netflix develops and applies advanced AI systems across internal workflows and member-facing products.

What you bring

  • Track record of research excellence in the post-training and alignment of foundation models and agentic systems, with expertise in areas such as reinforcement learning, preference optimization and reward modeling, reasoning and test-time inference, model distillation, agent scaffolding and evaluation, multi-agent systems, memory and long-horizon interaction, calibration and uncertainty, interpretability, robustness, or safety.

  • Ph.D. in a relevant area, with at least 2 years of post-Ph.D. experience in industry and/or academia.

  • Experience in applying research (especially your own) to transform real-world problems in collaboration with engineering and business teams.

  • Extensive research experience, in industry and/or academia, including as evidenced in top-tier publications.

  • Recognized for both technical expertise and the impact you drive, and trusted by stakeholders for collaboration, guidance, problem‑solving, and decision‑making.

  • Excellent judgment in identifying and framing ambiguous research and business problems and the links between the two.

  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate and build strong working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders to tackle big, cross-functional problems.

  • Effective communication with technical, non-technical, and mixed audiences.

  • Able to operate autonomously, take ownership in environments with minimal oversight, and lead work effectively with lightweight processes.

Content Infrastructure & Solutions (CIS) empowers engineers working on content, studio and enterprise applications to be innovative and agile in supporting Netflix's global content production needs. We do that by providing scalable and resilient infrastructure for large-scale media, assets, data, workflow and communication use cases.

Connected Enterprise Foundations (CEF), part of CIS, provides highly leveraged and fully managed data, search, workflow and messaging platforms for Content, Studio and Enterprise Engineering. CEF's charter is a connected enterprise experience: consistent, composable platform primitives that application teams and their agents build on, rather than a collection of separate products each with its own model of the world. Our sibling teams include Knowledge Foundations (data and domain modeling), Eventing and Communications Platform, Enterprise Workflow Platform, and the Enterprise Developer Paved Road.

About the team and the role

The AI Search Platform team owns Graph Search, Netflix’s enterprise search-as-a-service platform. Graph Search provides engineering teams with a unified way to index, search, and resolve entities across Content, Studio, Ads, and Enterprise. The team also builds and operates capabilities that enable internal users and agents to access the graph through natural language. It partners closely with the Knowledge Foundations team on the Unified Data Architecture, Data Dictionary, and Entity Graph.

The platform operates at significant scale today:

  • Approximately 19,500 weekly active users, more than double year over year

  • 13.5 million API calls per day, up 97% year over year

  • 233 production indices containing 13.3 billion documents, with index count up 74% year over year

  • More than 200 client applications consuming the search API, more than double year over year

You will lead a team of eight engineers based in Warsaw. The team has deep end-to-end ownership of the platform: it operates its own on-call, has delivered order-of-magnitude latency improvements across indexing and query paths, and has developed AI-powered operational tooling that has been adopted by other CIS teams.

The platform is at an inflection point, which makes this role particularly important:

  • From service to self-service. Graph Search is a powerful platform, but adoption is not yet effortless. Multi-tenancy, data product integration, and self-service onboarding are the next major steps.

  • From applications to primitives. The team has deliberately chosen not to build standalone end-user applications. Instead, it provides composable search primitives that enable other teams to build their own products, agents, and experiences while the team owns the underlying platform. Defining and maintaining that boundary, including evaluating when a use case does not belong on the platform, is a key part of the role.

  • Advance agentic and semantic search without neglecting the core. Agents are becoming first-class consumers of search, and semantic retrieval and entity grounding are major areas of investment. At the same time, keyword search remains the largest source of user value. The challenge is to advance the platform for emerging AI use cases without under-investing in the fundamentals that users depend on today.

  • Build a stronger discipline around impact. The team has an opportunity to become much more rigorous in connecting its investments to measurable business and organizational outcomes. Prioritization should be evidence-backed rather than strictly driven by inbound requests. You’ll also have the opportunity to shape how the team prioritizes its work and measures success.

Sr. Client Partner LATAM

At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.
 

With our ad-supported model live across LATAM and expanding into new markets, we are building a regional layer that helps our clients grow across countries, not just within them. We are looking for a founding-team member who will help shape how Netflix Ads works with regional clients across Latin America.

We are seeking a Senior Client Partner to lead the relationship with our priority regional clients across LATAM. This is not a single-market, direct-sales role, but it is a sales role at heart. We want someone with a strong commercial instinct who connects the dots across markets, thinks long term without losing sight of short and medium-term results, and works in a consultative way: understanding the client's business and leading the conversation, rather than pushing a product. The role sits at the center of many internal teams and works across markets with different priorities and ways of operating, so it takes diplomacy, poise and the ability to build alignment and keep things moving when interests compete. The ideal candidate is entrepreneurial, comfortable building where little exists yet, and skilled at influencing without formal authority. This role covers multiple countries and requires regular travel across the region.

Responsibilities

  • Own and grow the relationship with a portfolio of priority regional clients, acting as a strategic, consultative partner to their marketing leadership and media teams, and generating demand for Netflix that influences how they invest.

  • Connect local sales teams with global account teams, the export team, and cross-functional partners (Partner Marketing, Business Development, Brand Partnerships, Consumer Products, Live Experiences, Measurement, Policy and Legal), so regional clients get one coherent Netflix approach and their needs are met end to end.

  • Build data-informed account plans that grow top-line revenue, and align on objectives and priorities with regional leadership.

  • Build a proactive, year-round rhythm with clients through regular business reviews, education sessions, and data and audience conversations, so relationships deepen beyond individual negotiations.

  • Lead regional and multi-market opportunities end to end, coordinating the moving parts and keeping deals moving at pace.

  • Design projects and map the opportunities that make Netflix the one leading the CTV conversation, showing what streaming delivers across the full funnel and getting into clients' planning before the market does.

  • Put data, audience and programmatic at the center of the relationship, using first-party data and measurement to open larger, always-on opportunities.

  • Grow accounts beyond traditional media, into brand partnerships, product and licensing partnerships, and live events.

  • Use local results and case studies to build credibility, open regional doors, and build the pipeline for future years.

  • Keep Netflix top of mind in clients' regional planning, and stay current on industry trends and innovation to shape their strategies.

  • Map client stakeholders, media teams and agency leads, and stay close to the new regional structures clients are building.

  • Help build the regional way of working: create sales materials, playbooks and account rhythm that let a small team scale across markets, standardizing what can be reused instead of rebuilding per country.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years in advertising or media sales, or account management, with experience across more than one LATAM market or in a regional role.

  • A clear sales mindset: spots opportunities, connects them across markets, and grows accounts, balancing short and medium-term results with long-term relationships.

  • Considerable experience building and closing annual agreements and client JBPs.

  • Highly skilled in negotiating and selling the intrinsic value of a premium offering.

  • Proven strategic thinker who analyzes data and turns it into specific, measurable actions and outcomes.

  • A consultative approach: understands the client's business and leads the conversation with solutions rather than products. Comfortable with data, audience, programmatic and measurement, enough to go beyond the surface and ask the right questions.

  • Diplomacy and stakeholder management: keeps many teams aligned and moves work forward in complex, matrixed environments.

  • Comfort influencing stakeholders, across countries and teams that work in different ways.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and building process where little exists yet.

  • Excellent communication skills and strong, confident presentation skills.

  • Fluent in English and Spanish.

  • Availability and willingness to travel regularly across LATAM.

  • Ability to work in a dynamic, fast-paced setting, connect with cross-functional teams, and lead strategies in an ambiguous environment.

  • Comfortable using tools and AI to work efficiently and keep broad coverage with a lean team.

Preferred qualifications

  • Knowledge of the CTV and streaming landscape in LATAM.

  • Experience working with regional media teams or agency leads.

  • An established network across regional advertisers or their regional media teams.

It’s an exciting time to join Netflix as we continue shaping the future of global entertainment. We are looking to fill an integral role on the marketing team for a Marketing Manager - UK Film, based in London. This is a great opportunity for a passionate creative marketer with strong stakeholder management experience to join a team that leads the development and launch of marketing campaigns across a diverse range of feature films produced in the UK.

The Role

In this role, you will be a key contributor in strategising, executing and managing 360 marketing campaigns for Netflix films. We strive to not only build campaigns, but transform our properties into culturally relevant brands that connect with consumers and drive passionate followings. 

Core Responsibilities: 

  • Lead, and at times support, on launch campaigns for films being produced from the UK -- from global strategy development to creative execution, production to campaign rollout.

  • Drive and execute UK campaigns for international films, determining local strategy and crafting culturally relevant tactics 

  • Act as the creative champion with a holistic vision for leading campaigns, as well as being responsible for the day-to-day (including brief writing, shoot planning, budgeting and managing overall campaign resources)

  • Act as the central cross-functional liaison amongst internal teams (across region-based Marketing teams, PR, Publicity, Product and Social), with a focus on managing workflow and being able to share, review, organise and address cross-functional feedback

  • Act as the main point of contact with agencies - hire, manage and give feedback to create effective campaigns.

 

Who are we looking for?

This role is unique as it needs both a seasoned perspective and a team player attitude. The right candidate balances the vision and the people skills, the creative and the strategic. 

Must-have experience:

As part of the Infrastructure organization, the Engineering Enablement team helps scale Netflix’s engineering efficiency by improving how developers interact with core platform capabilities. We focus on strengthening developer workflows, optimizing platform usability, expanding paved-road tooling, and improving documentation and developer education. Our work combines hands-on technical investigation with platform-level influence.

Our Mission
Enable Netflix engineers to move quickly and confidently by improving their experience with the platform and by providing high-quality technical guidance across platform domains.

The Role

We’re looking for a Solutions Support Engineer to help Netflix engineers build, debug, and operate applications on our Python developer platform and paved paths.

This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who enjoys solving hard technical problems, improving developer workflows, and turning recurring issues into better tools and platform capabilities.

Your day-to-day

  • Debug complex issues across Python applications, frameworks, dependencies, CI/CD, runtime environments, and platform integrations.

  • Experience with Python frameworks and development tooling such as FastAPI, Flask

  • Hands-on experience using AI coding assistants and agentic tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, MCP) to troubleshoot, automate, and accelerate engineering work.

  • Interest in improving developer productivity and making engineering workflows more effective at scale.

Experience in one or more of the following:

Who We Are We are the JavaScript Foundations (JSF) team in Warsaw. The Enterprise Data Science & Engineering (DSE) team’s mission is to make Netflix technologists more productive and our enterprise data stronger and more connected. We achieve this through dedicated data products and deep partnerships that leverage our data expertise.

We are driving a major initiative to deepen data excellence across the organization. Our focus is on enabling high-quality data foundations that support next-generation tools and internal productivity products, ensuring our data ecosystem remains robust and scalable as the business grows.

We are looking for a Analytics Engineer to lead the analytics strategy for Data Health at Netflix.

This role leans heavily into analytics and strategy. While engineering skills are required to access and model data, the primary focus is on defining measurement frameworks. You will be a thought leader responsible for conceptualizing what "healthy data" looks like across diverse domains and translating abstract concepts like "trust," "availability," or "compliance" into concrete, actionable metrics.

As an Analytics Engineer, you will act as a cross functional lead, partnering with Engineering Leaders, Product Managers, and other DSE teams to establish comprehensive visibility into the state of Netflix’s data ecosystem.

What You Will Do

  • Define Data Excellence Metrics: You will lead the development of advanced quality indicators, moving beyond standard availability checks to define complex measures of data health.

  • Build the Analytical Foundation: Design and implement the data models and dashboards that will serve as the trusted source for understanding the health of our critical data assets. You will be responsible for visualizing the state of our data landscape for executive leadership.

  • Drive Strategy through Insights: Use data to influence engineering behavior and investment. You will analyze trends in lineage, asset utilization, and data lifecycle to identify opportunities for high-impact improvements across Netflix.

  • Partner on Platform Capabilities: Collaborate with Data Platform engineering teams to ensure our infrastructure and orchestration tools emit the necessary metadata and telemetry to support sophisticated health analysis.

  • Connect the Dots: Work across domain-centric workstreams to standardize how we evaluate data quality, ensuring consistent definitions and standards apply across the company.

  • Measure Impact: Develop metrics to track the success of our data initiatives, focusing on improvements in developer productivity, reduction in data friction, and the adoption of standardized tooling.


What We Are Looking For

  • Analytical Leadership: You excel at defining metrics in complex spaces. You are adept at asking "what should the data be telling us?" and can build novel measurement frameworks where standard metrics may not yet exist.

  • Seniority & Influence: You have experience driving large-scale initiatives. You can communicate complex data concepts to non-technical stakeholders and influence technical teams to prioritize data quality work based on your analytical findings.

  • Technical Proficiency: High proficiency in SQL and Python is essential. You are comfortable building your own pipelines and utilizing modern data stack tools to unblock your analysis and prototype solutions.

  • Strategic Thinking: You can balance the delivery of immediate analytical insights with the long-term vision of a robust, automated data health ecosystem.

  • Build strong partnerships with key regional organizations and represent Netflix at industry and company events.
     

Operational & Financial Excellence

  • Drive standardization and continuous improvement of localization workflows, ensuring creative, technical, and operational excellence.

  • Partner with Finance and Accounting to track and manage local localization, dubbing, and subtitling costs, monitoring market trends and union/guild activity.

Thought Leadership & Innovation

  • Identify opportunities for growth, quality improvement, and scalability within localization, dubbing, and subtitling operations.

  • Contribute to Netflix’s culture of curiosity, responsibility, and innovation, sharing best practices and learnings across regions.

  • Deliver impactful analyses and presentations to executive audiences, translating complex ideas into actionable insights.

This role will be part of Brand Partnerships, a team responsible for developing and disseminating solutions for a growing set of global advertising partners, eager to unlock the value of our IP and distinct advertising products and services that only a global streaming leader can offer.

About The Role:  

The Manager of Brand Partnerships, Title Management: Sports will lead the team responsible for developing and delivering brand partnerships that drive commercial outcomes tied to our ambitious sports slate.  This person will work directly with rights holders and our Sports Content team to extract maximum commercial value through sponsorships, editorial features, product innovation, custom content and bespoke partnerships.  To be successful in this role the candidate will need to have experience working with a broad set of sports leagues and production entities.  You will lead the development of our turnkey and bespoke commercial packages and oversee their implementation with our internal production and creative teams.   This role will require someone with a background in activating sponsorships and integrations tied to sports (both live and docu-series), a deep understanding of live event production logistics, and experience working with advertising clients in live and SVOD content environments.   

You will be a trusted resource for understanding what brand partners can be authentic to the creative vision of our live events.  This person will need to build effective relationships with external production companies, ad sales, and clients to bring these programs to life.  This role will also work closely with key stakeholders in our Title Marketing, Live Production, Social, Production, Creative, Streaming Product and other relevant areas of the business to ensure we are developing robust offerings to drive growth in our ad business. 

This person will deploy the offerings to our sales team. 

This role presents a huge opportunity to be at the forefront of a new Netflix offering, one that continues to prove how Netflix is the most innovative entertainment company in the world and grows an important new revenue stream for the business. Our Data Platform team provides centralized data platforms and tools for various business functions at Netflix, enabling them to utilize data to make critical, data-driven decisions. We focus on making it easy for our business partners to work with data efficiently, securely, and responsibly. We aspire to set the industry standard in building a world-class data infrastructure, supporting Netflix’s goal to be the most popular and widely accessible destination for global internet entertainment.


As the Data Platform charter grows, we are expanding our presence to Poland to further increase our impact. We are seeking Distributed Systems Engineers to help evolve and innovate our Product and Infrastructure. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team that brings new perspectives as we address the next set of challenges.


Team Spotlights


Analytics Platform and Experience Team

This team owns the architecture and foundational systems of Netflix's Analytics Platform, a growing domain with an expanding charter as the platform scales to support critical initiatives like Live and Ads. The team currently owns automated Spark migration tooling and TableDiff, our in-house data validation tool used both as a critical enabler for migrations and as a widely adopted utility across the org. As the charter grows, the team will take on additional high-impact platform initiatives. This offers an excellent opportunity to shape foundational data infrastructure and deliver direct, high-leverage impact across Netflix


Data Movement Team

The Data Movement Connector EcoSystem at Netflix is a growing domain with an expanding charter to own high-leverage business-critical connectors across Netflix. The team currently offers Frameworks, Libraries, and Control Planes and supports a large set of streaming/incremental and batch/snapshot-based connectors. This offering evolves the next step is full ownership of the Mantis ecosystem. We believe having the Poland team build and own a set of connectors to move and integrate data across different business domains would be the fastest way to unlock business values. This offers an excellent opportunity to learn the technology stack and deliver direct, relevant impact across the organization.


Online Data Stores Team

This team takes end-to-end ownership of Netflix's internal Online Data Stores (ODS) platform, spanning two core areas:

1. Core data platform products

Ownership of critical infrastructure such as ZooKeeper and the data abstraction layers that sit on top of our datastores - ensuring their reliability, scalability, and continued evolution as foundational components of the data platform.

2. Self-service solutions for Online Data Stores

Building the self-service capabilities - including agentic interfaces - that let Netflix engineers provision, operate, and reason about their datastores independently, reducing operational friction and toil.

Over time the team will expand its charter to additional datastores and broader infrastructure initiatives. The mission throughout is to boost Netflix engineers' productivity and innovation through a robust, efficient, and secure data platform, while fostering close collaboration across data platform teams to deliver greater organizational throughput and agility.


Experimentation Platform Team

This team owns the data infrastructure that makes A/B testing work at Netflix. Specifically, they build and maintain the systems that store and govern the record of who was in which experiment, across hundreds of concurrent tests running across streaming, ads, growth, and device platforms. They also own the semantic layer that ties every experiment metric at Netflix back to that allocation data, and the pipelines that keep the whole thing fresh and reliable. As the team matures, the scope grows to include self-service tooling for the teams running experiments and support for AI-driven monitoring and analysis workflows.

Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

 

The Product Merchandising team connects members to Netflix's world of entertainment by blending intuitive merchandising and market expertise to position, promote, and present content so members find it easy and enjoyable to choose what they'll love. 

The Product Merchandising Team UK and Nordics positions our local award-winning, industry-leading content for distribution on the Netflix service through our work on individual titles as well as the broader catalogue in our markets. 

The Role

Product Merchandising blends intuitive merchandising strategy and deep local expertise to position, promote, and present content — making it easy and enjoyable for every Netflix member to choose what they'll love. We're blending global scale with deep local expertise, and we're looking for people who can bring both. 

As a Merchandiser, you shape the merchandising experience for Netflix members in your markets — across creative, editorial, and catalog dimensions. You are a platform-first impact driver: someone who shapes how the Netflix experience looks, reads, and feels for members in the UK across every surface, every content format, and every moment. 

What You'll Do

Shape the Local Member Experience 

  • Drive the local UK merchandising calendar — planning activations around title launches, cultural moments, seasonal trends, and member lifecycle milestones throughout the year.

  • Lead distribution and promotion strategy for local title launches — from positioning and merchandising strategy through to post-launch performance.

  • Propose, develop  and execute catalog activations (rows, hubs, custom promotions) that drive content discovery and reflect what resonates culturally with consumers in your market.

  • Develop messaging campaigns — push notifications, emails — that connect members to content they'll love, timed to the moments and titles that matter locally.

  • Editorialize catalog content beyond new launches to support member engagement, surfacing library titles and hidden gems at the right point in the member journey. Partner with cross functional stakeholders to drive business impact at the local level through this work.

  • Connect the dots between platform logic, consumer insights, and content strategy to drive strong merchandising activations and learning agendas. 

  • Apply deep awareness of local trends, social and cultural zeitgeist, and platform behavior to shape what gets surfaced, when, and how — in close partnership with Marketing and Comms.

  • Advocate for your market's needs in regional and global conversations, sharing context that cross-functional partners cannot access without you.

  • Work closely with Content, Marketing, Product teams, and external agency partners to proactively share context, surface trade-offs, and align on priorities to deliver a cohesive member experience.

  • Operate within global governance frameworks and playbooks, ensuring local activations complement the global calendar.

  • Act as the local intelligence layer to surface on-the-ground market insights and trends, and contribute to playbooks and standards that can be scaled across markets in partnership with local Consumer Insights and Content Strategy.

Creative & Editorial 

  • Partner with local marcomms on Product Title Creative Assets for priority titles, using external agencies where additional assets may be required. Briefing and reviewing imagery, copy, and promotional materials. 

  • Ensure Product Assets across image, AV and copy adhere to Netflix's standards for quality, consistency, and local authenticity.

  • Operate within the global Merchandising Playbook while driving locally resonant decisions. 

  • Use AV where needed to deepen member engagement across the title lifecycle and provide clear, actionable feedback to ensure output meets positioning, creative guidelines, and timelines.

  • Partner with Creative Services and Design to ensure assets perform across all devices, with particular mastery of mobile as a primary discovery canvas in the UK.

  • Optimize consumer messaging (email, push, in-app notifications) that feels genuinely individual — tailored to member behavior and lifestyle signals, not generic promotional copy.

Turn Data into insights to drive better experiences

  • Partner with regional Performance Analysts and Technical Merchandising to monitor and report on activations at the local level. Ensure hypotheses created at the local level are reflected in data gathered post launch. 

  • Contribute to A/B testing and experimentation, using data, dashboards, analytics tools alongside qualitative market insight to continuously improve the member experience.

  • Think in business outcomes, not just creative outputs: track and communicate the impact of merchandising decisions on member engagement, viewing behavior, and platform health metrics to your peers and cross-functional partners.

  • Write clear, well-reasoned strategic briefs that articulate the why behind your activation decisions and earn alignment from partners and leadership.

  • Fluency in business metrics and translating them to merchandising strategy. You understand the UK business inside out, think member-first, and know how to bridge both to achieve ambitious business impact. 

  • Work at pace: move from concept to live activation quickly while maintaining quality and intentionality.

What We're Looking For

  • A proven ability to engage customers via digital promotional and/or merchandising tactics, driving product engagement in an authentic and culturally relevant manner. 

  • Deep cultural fluency in the UK and curiosity to learn about new ones. You understand what resonates, what's trending, and what UK members respond to.

  • A strong track record of using data to make decisions — you're comfortable reading consumer insight studies, dashboards, spotting patterns, and translating insights into action.

  • Experience writing strategic briefs: you can define a problem clearly, build hypotheses, stress-test your own assumptions before making a recommendation with conviction, and bring stakeholders along.

  • Operational excellence: you're organized and accurate under high-volume, fast-moving conditions.

  • Think in systems: you instinctively connect content, members, product behavior, and market context into a coherent picture, and you know which questions to ask to fill in the gaps before forming a view.

  • A collaborative approach: you work well across functions, time zones, and seniority levels, and you know when to push back and when to align.

  • Genuinely love entertainment: you are an avid consumer of content across film, series, and beyond, and you bring real passion and taste to the work.

  • Native or full professional fluency in [local language(s)] and English; mastery of [local] editorial and cultural standards.

We are looking for a Coordinator who can help turn the team’s initiative into coordinated, sustained action. Reporting to and working in close partnership with the Director, Creative Strategy – APAC (ex-India), you will be an early member of a lean team, helping connect projects, people, and priorities across markets. You will create visibility across a growing portfolio of work, ensure that important context travels, and help regional initiatives move forward with clarity and momentum.

This is a unique opportunity to play a meaningful role in shaping how the function operates while gaining a broad view of how content and creative teams work across APAC. The role is grounded in project coordination and operational execution: bringing structure to complexity, anticipating what the team needs, and ensuring that ideas and commitments translate into clear next steps and meaningful follow-through. You will thrive in this role if you enjoy connecting the dots across different markets and cultures, are energized by building something new, and recognize that different contexts call for different answers. You are comfortable adapting your approach as needs evolve and take pride in enabling others to do their best creative work.
 

| Core Responsibilities:

  • Track and coordinate Creative Strategy’s active projects, title engagements, and regional initiatives across APAC (ex-India), maintaining clear visibility into stakeholders, status, timelines, dependencies, deliverables, and next steps, while proactively surfacing gaps or potential delays

  • Translate the team’s priorities, ideas, and commitments into clear actions and projects, driving coordinated execution and sustained follow-through across markets

  • Coordinate scheduling, communications, and information flow across Creative Strategy, local Content teams, cross-functional partners, and global teams, preparing agendas, presentations, and briefs that clearly capture context, decisions, and next steps

  • Track relevant internal slates, new releases, competitive activity, and partner developments across APAC, and compile the information and research to support team projects and regional initiatives

  • The ability to bring structure to ambiguity and establish practical ways of working in a lean, newly established team, where processes and priorities will continue to evolve.

  • Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to work thoughtfully across different teams, markets, and cultures.
